findings.claim: Every retired memory that has a page is visited and counted as patched on every later run, because PatchStatusFields is idempotent but not change-aware. The summary says `patched N page(s)` and the dry run lists `would patch` for pages already patched, indefinitely. An operator cannot tell a real change from a no-op, and the dry-run prediction is always non-zero once any memory is retired. The log and docs acknowledge this as Engram parity, but it is still a misleading count introduced for the memorycard path.
proof_refs: propagate_cards.go eachCardPatchTarget calls visit for every scan.own page with no changed-check
docs/sync-from-memorycard.md: 'A page already patched is visited again and rewrites nothing... the run counts it.'

findings.claim: If ListRetiredMemories fails after the promotion pass has written pages, SyncCardsProject returns MemoryUnavailable before the index rebuild and the sync-state record. Before this change, the same run rebuilt and recorded after promotion. The comment says rebuild and record happen even when a memory fails, but this new early return makes the promoted pages unindexed until the next successful run.
proof_refs: sync_cards.go: `case CardRunFailure(patchErr) == MemoryUnavailable: ... return out, patchErr` sits before the RebuildIndex call

findings.claim: Propagation walks only the superseded and archived memories. A memory that memorycard returns to `active` keeps its page at `superseded` or `archived`, because the promotion pass sees no new revision and the retired listing no longer includes it. Nothing patches the status back.
